data.description:
## The pathology

`with TestClient(app)` — the CONTEXT-MANAGER form — runs the review-bot app's LIFESPAN. That starts the queue worker, the REAL backfill reconciler and the snapshot janitor, and on exit awaits `queue.join()` under `shutdown_drain_seconds()`, which defaults to **1200 seconds** (`review_bot/config.py:49`, `:92-103`).

A test that constructs an ASGI client the idiomatic way therefore inherits a 20-minute shutdown drain plus a real filesystem sweep. Nothing in the test surface warns about it.

## Proven, not theorised

Diagnosed during ticket 9f63 (Gerrit change 1512) by A/B against a clean tree — this is attribution, not correlation:
* clean `origin/main` @`1afdbbd0be`, CI's exact py3.11 command (coverage + xdist): **11184 passed, 16m11s**
* the SAME command on a tree whose only difference was a `/health` test using `with TestClient(app)`: **hung at 99%**

`faulthandler` (`timeout -s ABRT`) showed a worker holding a live anyio blocking portal alongside a thread in `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:282 startup_sweep` -> `src/rebar/_snapshot/cache.py:133 entry_size`. Fixed there by awaiting the `health()` handler directly instead of constructing a client: **11197 passed, 13m33s**.

## Why the existing mitigations are not enough

**The per-test hang guard (landed today, `f47acb7051`, ticket 89d5) makes this VISIBLE, not IMPOSSIBLE.** `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` plus faulthandler now names the hung test in ~5 minutes instead of eating the full 60-minute job in silence. That is a large improvement and it is why this ticket is about PREVENTION only — the detection half is done.

**The current safe pattern is unenforced per-test discipline.** The three lifespan-entering tests that behave each hand-roll the same two stubs — `monkeypatch.setattr(appmod._reconcile, "reconcile_loop", _idle_reconcile_loop)` and a `start_background_janitor` stub (`tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1446-1449`, with `_idle_reconcile_loop` at `:1423`). A fourth author has no way to know that is required. That is exactly what happened.

**Nothing bounds the drain globally in tests.** A grep of `tests/` finds `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` set only inside one test that is specifically about the drain (`test_review_bot.py:1478`, to "0.1"). There is no floor for everything else.

## The work

**1. Bound the drain for the whole test suite.** `shutdown_drain_seconds()` ALREADY reads `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` from the environment, validates it, and falls back safely on a missing/unparseable/non-positive value. Set it to a small value in the test conftest. This requires NO production change — it uses a knob the code already exposes — and it protects every test whether or not its author knew about the stubs.

**2. Make the stubbed path the default in that module.** An autouse fixture applying both stubs, so entering the lifespan is safe by default and a test that genuinely wants the real loop opts OUT explicitly. Removes the per-test discipline that failed here.

## Explicitly NOT doing: an AST lint

Flagging `with TestClient(app)` statically was considered and rejected. The signal is poor: `TestClient` can be aliased, wrapped in a fixture, or built indirectly, and the rule is not 'never enter the lifespan' but 'entering it requires stubs' — a relationship between statements that AST matching handles badly. It would produce false positives on legitimate tests, false negatives on indirect construction, and need maintaining forever. Items 1 and 2 remove the pathology instead of detecting it, using mechanisms the code already provides.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The test suite bounds `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` globally, so no test can inherit the 1200s drain
- [ ] The PRODUCTION default remains 1200s and is still pinned by a test, so bounding it under test cannot mask a real drain regression (`test_review_bot.py:1521` already asserts against `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` — confirm it still does)
- [ ] The drain-specific test that sets its own value (`:1478`) still controls its own value and is not overridden by the global bound
- [ ] Entering the app lifespan in that module is safe BY DEFAULT via an autouse fixture; the three existing hand-rolled stub sites are migrated to it rather than left duplicated
- [ ] A test that wants the REAL reconcile loop can opt out explicitly, and at least one does so, proving the escape hatch works
- [ ] A RED oracle: a test that enters the lifespan WITHOUT any hand-rolled stub completes promptly, and fails against the pre-fix tree
data.title: Entering the review-bot app lifespan in a test inherits a 1200s shutdown drain — bound it in tests and make the stubbed path the default
